classes_covered: secrets (hardcoded keys, service_role by value, DB creds in headers, seeder credentials)
supabase RLS (missing RLS, USING(true), views, SECURITY DEFINER, policy scoping, storage.objects, verify_jwt, dashboard drift via --schema)
next.js auth basics (tokens in web storage, cookie flags, NEXT_PUBLIC secrets, mutating endpoints without in-file auth)
nestjs playbook (APP_GUARD-aware unguarded controllers, CORS, helmet, throttler)
sast-light (SQLi concat, XSS dangerous HTML, eval/exec, weak hashing)
dependencies (CVEs vs bundled advisory snapshot, known-malicious, typosquat, unresolved-no-lockfile, slopsquat via --online)
ci/supply-chain (GitHub Actions SHA pinning, pull_request_target, script injection, permissions; Dockerfile root/:latest/ARG secrets)
recon inventory (routes, server actions, controllers w/ guards, supabase tables/RPC/edge functions, socket events, webhooks)
taint-lite (SSRF, open redirect, path traversal, command injection, reflected XSS — single-file scope, MEDIUM cap, generated canary tests)
rule packs II (LOGS-001, SUPA-002/003, AUTH-001 middleware-matcher gaps, NEXT-005 CSRF heuristic, MASS-001, WS-001, WEBHOOK-001, JWT-001/002, SWAGGER-001, PRISMA-001 hint)
agent environment (unpinned MCP servers, secrets in agent configs, permission wildcards/bypass, unpinned hook commands)
AI review layer with independent verifier (opt-in --ai-review; redaction-before-LLM; verifier-gated; AI findings cap at HIGH)
authz matrix + generated Supertest/Playwright quarantine tests (test-authz — the tool never executes them)
agent guard hook (init-hook — PreToolUse prevention of service_role-in-client, RLS-killing SQL, secrets into .env)
classes_not_covered: deep multi-file taint flows (taint-lite is single-file + one-level import by design)
IDOR differential testing / authz matrix execution (v1.0 — restricted; the generated tests are run by the owner, never the tool)
URL Mode L1–L3: security headers, exposed files, live probing (v0.4 — after Mode 1 completes)
cookie HttpOnly deep verification beyond the flag-level check + full CSRF semantics (heuristic only)
business & payment logic (human review by design)
non-JS/TS languages (non-goal — use the Semgrep adapter)

findings.title: Workflow uses pull_request_target (fork code with repo secrets)

evidence.note: combined with checkout of the PR head this executes fork code in a privileged context

findings.fix: Avoid pull_request_target with checkout of the PR head: fork code would run with repository secrets. If you must label/comment, checkout the base ref and never execute untrusted PR code in a privileged job.

findings.title: Workflow grants write-all permissions

evidence.note: every token in this workflow can write repos/packages — least privilege required

findings.fix: Grant least-privilege: set the top-level permissions block explicitly (e.g. contents: read) and add only the scopes a job truly needs (security-events: write for SARIF upload). Avoid permissions: write-all.

findings.title: Untrusted event data interpolated directly into run: script (block)

evidence.note: a crafted PR title/branch name becomes shell code with workflow-token access

findings.fix: Never interpolate untrusted event data (titles, bodies, branch names) directly into run: scripts. Pass the value through the environment: env: TITLE: ${{ ... }} then use "$TITLE" quoted inside the script.

findings.title: jwt.decode() feeds an authorization decision — decode does NOT verify the signature

evidence.masked: const payload = jwt.decode(token) as { role?: string; sub?: string } | null;
evidence.note: anyone can craft a token with any role/claim — jwt.decode trusts it blindly

findings.fix: Use jwt.verify(token, secret, { algorithms: [...] }) — verification first; only then read claims for decisions.

evidence.note: a renamed or hijacked package replaces the tool your agent runs with — pin the exact version

findings.fix: Pin the exact version (e.g. "supa-db-mcp@1.4.2") or install it as a dev dependency and reference the local binary. Never @latest in agent config.

findings.title: Agent hook executes remote/unpinned code — hooks run automatically on every tool call

evidence.note: hooks are the agent's pre-execution gate — pointing them at unpinned packages hands the gate to npm

findings.fix: Commit the hook script into the repo (pinned by version control) and invoke it locally (node .claude/hooks/<script>.mjs) — never npx/@latest inside hook config.

findings.title: Mutating endpoint without in-file auth check (middleware exists — verify matcher coverage)

evidence.note: middleware.ts present — middleware-only auth is fragile (matchers drift); confirm server-side check

findings.fix: Add an explicit server-side auth check at the top of the handler (verify the session/token server-side, not just middleware), and reject unauthenticated mutations with 401.

findings.title: User-controlled value flows into a shell command string — command injection

evidence.note: exec(`convert ${req.query.file}`) — ';' or '$(...)' in the query executes as shell

findings.fix: Never interpolate user input into shell strings — use execFile/spawn with an argv array (shell: false) and validate the input against an allowlist.

findings.title: User-controlled value flows into an outbound request URL — SSRF (server can be pointed anywhere)

evidence.note: classic vibe-coding SSRF: 'fetch anything by URL' helpers — internal services/metadata IPs become reachable

findings.fix: Validate the destination against a host allowlist (scheme + exact host) before any outbound request; block private/link-local ranges (169.254.x, 127.x, 10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x) and metadata endpoints.

findings.title: User-controlled value flows into a redirect target — open redirect (phishing pivot)

evidence.note: redirect(req.query.to) sends users anywhere — tokens/refs in the URL leak to attacker sites

findings.fix: Only redirect to relative paths (reject absolute URLs and protocol-relative //host), or validate the target against an origin allowlist before redirecting.

findings.title: Container runs as root (no USER directive)

evidence.note: add a non-root user and switch before the runtime stage

findings.fix: Run the container as a non-root user: add a dedicated user in the Dockerfile (USER app) or set runAsNonRoot in the deployment. Root containers escalate container escapes.

findings.title: Base image pinned to :latest (mutable)
findings.fix: Pin base images by digest or at least a specific version tag — :latest is mutable and breaks reproducibility; a registry compromise silently changes your base.

findings.title: "some-madeup-util" cannot be resolved offline and the project has no lockfile

evidence.note: no lockfile proves this package ever resolved — hallucinated/slopsquat candidates land here; re-run with --online to check the registry

findings.fix: Verify "some-madeup-util" exists on the npm registry and is the package you intend. Generate a lockfile (npm install --package-lock-only) so dependency resolution becomes reproducible and auditable.

findings.title: Policy "everyone_read" on users has no user scoping (auth.uid())

evidence.note: any authenticated client may satisfy this policy — scoping to auth.uid() (or a role check) is expected on user-data tables

findings.fix: Scope the policy: USING (auth.uid() = user_id) (or the correct ownership column), or restrict it TO a specific role.

findings.title: Buckets created in migrations but no storage.objects RLS policies found

evidence.note: bucket inserts alone do not protect object access — public/anon policies must exist deliberately

findings.fix: Add explicit storage.objects policies (e.g. USING (bucket_id = 'x' AND auth.role() = 'authenticated')) or confirm the bucket is intentionally public-read.

findings.title: CORS allows any origin
findings.fix: Restrict CORS to an explicit origin allowlist (cors: { origin: [...], credentials: true }). origin: '*' lets any website read authenticated responses from your API.

findings.title: User-controlled value flows into a filesystem path — path traversal (../../ out of the data dir)

evidence.note: path.join(base, req.params.file) with ../../etc/passwd escapes the base dir

findings.fix: Resolve the final path and assert it is still inside the intended root (path.resolve + startsWith(root)), or reduce the input to path.basename() before joining.

findings.title: User-controlled value flows into server-rendered HTML — reflected XSS

evidence.note: template HTML with ${req.query.x} — script payloads execute in the victim's browser

findings.fix: Escape the value before it enters HTML (or render as text, never raw HTML); if HTML is required, sanitize server-side with an allowlist-based sanitizer.

findings.title: helmet() not registered — security headers missing
findings.fix: Register helmet() (app.use(helmet())) so security headers (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frameguard) are set on every response.

findings.title: No rate limiting found (ThrottlerModule / rate-limit)
findings.fix: Add ThrottlerModule + APP_GUARD ThrottlerGuard (or express-rate-limit) so login/OTP/auth routes resist brute force.

findings.title: Swagger/OpenAPI UI served without a production guard — full API surface is public
findings.fix: Serve Swagger only outside production: if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production") SwaggerModule.setup(...).

findings.title: .gitignore missing entries: .env, *.pem / SSH keys, *.tfstate
findings.fix: Add .env, *.pem / SSH keys, *.tfstate to .gitignore to prevent accidental commits.
